_meta.purpose: Nano banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image via fal.ai) prompts for real-photo/richly-illustrated gallery images to power photo-diagram hotspot skills for Grade 5. Grade 5 currently has only two subjects built as skill files — Mathematics (web/src/skills/mathG5/) and Science & Technology (web/src/skills/scienceG5/) — and Grade 5 has NO images at all yet. Sourced from a visual-coverage audit (2026-08-29) that read every shipped Grade 5 Science skill file's own content pools against curriculum-reference/grade-5/science-and-technology.json (mined per CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md) and checked each existing SVG VisualSpec type in the codebase before proposing anything new, per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md and the SVG-check rule. Mathematics was deliberately given ZERO images this batch: every Grade 5 Math sub-strand audited (Numbers, Measurement, Geometry) is either purely abstract/numeric (place value, the four operations, fractions, decimals) or already has strong non-photo visual support — 3-D objects (cube/cuboid/cylinder/sphere/pyramid) already have interactive `solid-rotate` support per curriculum-reference/grade-5/mathematics.json's own note, and Volume (2.3) is stacked-cube-array content that SVG already handles well — so no genuinely strong real-world-object case existed, and the brief explicitly says not to pad Math without one.
updateLog: 2026-08-29 initial batch: 10 images, all Science & Technology (sci-g5-*), 0 Mathematics (no genuine photo-diagram gap found — see purpose note above). Every image targets a sub-strand where a shipped skill's branches are currently pure text/name-sorting with zero visual grounding (classificationOfPlants.ts, vertebrates.ts, mixtures.ts, waterPollution.ts, floatingAndSinking.ts, heatTransfer.ts, soundEnergy.ts) and where a real photograph-style gallery is genuinely better than a code-drawn SVG per the task brief's own examples: real organism galleries (vertebrates, flowering/non-flowering plants), a real multi-object comparison panel (floating vs sinking objects, good vs poor heat conductors — mirroring the proven pretech-g9-wood-samples pattern), and real-world scene galleries (water pollution sources, water treatment methods, mixture separation methods, mixture homogeneous/heterogeneous examples, sound sources). humanBreathingSystem.ts was deliberately left with no new image: its parts (nose, trachea, lungs, diaphragm) are already served by an existing SVG 'respiratory-system' schematic diagram type, which is the medically appropriate way to show internal anatomy for this age group — a real photo would be either inappropriate (real lung/organ photography) or add no clarity over the existing labelled schematic. Every gallery image follows the grid-of-bordered-single-item-panels lesson learned in the Grade 6 batch (never a shared busy scene for 4+ items) and every prompt explicitly forbids printing any part's name as text, matching this file's criticalRule.
howToUse: 1. Copy one entry's `prompt` field verbatim into fal.ai (nano banana / Gemini 2.5 Flash Image).
2. Save the returned image, then tell Claude which `id` it corresponds to and where the file was saved.

3. Claude will inspect the image with vision to confirm every letter actually printed on the image matches an item in that entry's `expectedLabels`, note (and skip, not guess) any duplicated/ambiguous printed letters, run `npm run images:webp` (from web/) to convert the source PNG to WebP in place, add/reuse an entry in the shared cross-skill registry `web/src/lib/photoImages.ts` (never inline the image/part data directly in a skill file), wire a multi-Bloom's-tier set of question branches into the skill file(s) named in `targetSkillFile` per RIGOR-STANDARDS.md, and verify (tsc + lint + a real request against the running dev server) before calling it done.

4. If any part is missing an arrow/letter, or a letter's arrow lands on the wrong structure, regenerate with a corrected prompt (add an explicit correction line naming the missing/misplaced part) rather than accepting a partial image — every part in `expectedLabels` must be identifiable.

5. An image is not tied to the one skill in `targetSkillFile` — once registered in photoImages.ts, reuse it from any other skill (same or different subject, same grade) that has a genuine curriculum reason to reference it, per curriculum-reference/CURRICULUM-MINING-GUIDE.md's photo-diagram section.
_meta.styleGuideSummary: All prompts embed the same style block so every generated image reads as one consistent visual system across the whole app — do not vary the style between images.
_meta.criticalRule: Every prompt instructs nano banana NOT to print any part's name as text anywhere on the image — only a circled capital letter + thin leader line per part. This is deliberate and different from typical stock 'labeled diagram' images (which usually print full text labels): text labels would give the answer away before the question is even asked. If a returned image has any part's name printed as text, it must be regenerated.
_meta.displayConstraint: Confirmed in web/src/components/visuals/Visual.tsx's PhotoDiagram renderer: images display at max-height 420px, max-width 672px (Tailwind max-w-2xl), object-contain, width 100% of container. Source images at roughly 1024-1200px on the long edge are plenty — this is never a print asset. The `dimensions` field on each entry below states the generation aspect ratio/size that best fits that constraint.

The letters, in reading order, are: Panel 1 (winnowing) = A, Panel 2 (picking) = B, Panel 3 (sieving) = C, Panel 4 (magnet) = D, Panel 5 (filtering) = E, Panel 6 (decanting) = F, Panel 7 (separating funnel) = G.
